# Model inputs

## Generated by `case.setup`

| file | content |
|---|---|
| `FE_Global.txt` | mesh mode, number of faults, friction law, time step, cycle range, friction, material, loading and output switches |
| `FE_Model_Geometry.txt` | domain extension, mesh coarsening ratio, cell size |
| `FE_Fault_Geometry.txt` | per-fault geometry control |

Do not edit these by hand; edit `user_defined_params.py` and re-run
`case.setup`.

## Fault geometry

* **C_mesh = 2:** `x1_1.txt`, `x2_1.txt`, … — one file per fault, two
  columns, x and y in km in the model frame, x strictly increasing. The
  solver fits a natural cubic spline through them; `ftcn` gives the number of
  points per fault.
* **C_mesh = 3:** `user_fault_geometry_input/*.gmt.txt`, one file per fault,
  x and y in km; `meshgen.py` meshes them with gmsh.

## Tectonic loading

Between earthquakes, each fault node's stress relaxes towards an asymptotic
state set by the local shear strain rate γ and the angle of compression φ
(local fault strike minus the maximum-shear-strain-rate direction):

```
shear  ->  s γ cos(2φ) η
normal ->  -s γ sin(2φ) η + σ_ambient
```

with a viscosity η = η₀ · γ_ref / γ, so the asymptotic stress does not depend
on γ and γ only sets how fast it is approached. s is `par.slipSense`: +1
(default) drives right-lateral slip, −1 left-lateral. For s = +1, positive φ
clamps the fault (more compression) and negative φ unclamps it; for s = −1 the
reverse.

**Slip sense comes only from `slipSense`.** `ftType` (column 4 of
`nsmpGeoPhys.txt`) is written but never read by the solver, so before
`slipSense` existed every fault was simulated right-lateral. One value
applies to the whole system.

For s = −1, measure φ from the **left-lateral** maximum-shear plane, with
angles counter-clockwise: in the frame where the strain-rate tensor is E and
the fault has unit tangent t and left normal n, γ cos 2φ = −tᵀEn (left-lateral
resolved shear) and γ sin 2φ = nᵀEn − tr(E)/2 (deviatoric normal, extension
positive). The `strain_rate_loading.py` scripts in the GSRM compsets compute
φ this way.

### C_mesh = 2: `Rate_direction.txt`

`maxftnode × ntotft` rows, two columns: γ in s⁻¹ and φ in degrees, per fault
node. Format, units and code path: `compset/paper.saf.A/RATE_DIRECTION.md`.

### C_mesh = 3: `nsmpGeoPhys.txt`

`maxftnode × ntotft` rows, nine columns:

| col | name | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 1, 2 | `tx`, `ty` | unit fault tangent |
| 3 | `len` | segment length, m |
| 4 | `ftType` | 1 left-lateral, −1 right-lateral, 2 thrust, −2 normal; not read by the solver, see `slipSense` |
| 5 | `ftDip` | dip, degrees (90 = vertical strike-slip) |
| 6 | `ftLoadMaxShear` | shear strain rate γ, s⁻¹ |
| 7 | `ftLoadAngle` | φ, degrees; −999 = take it from the fault tangent |
| 8 | `ftLoadWt` | loading weight, default 450; only sets the approach timescale |
| 9 | `ftVis` | viscosity η, Pa·s |

### Choosing the loading stress

The asymptotic shear stress T = γ·η must not exceed the magnitude of the
ambient normal stress N where the loading unclamps the fault (φ < 0 for
s = +1, φ > 0 for s = −1), or those nodes are driven tensile. In general the
asymptotic normal stress is −N − s·T·sin 2φ, so every node stays below the
−10 MPa cap for T ≤ (N − 10 MPa) / max(−s·sin 2φ). A fault whose angle of compression is coherently positive (the San
Andreas, 91% of nodes) tolerates T/N ≈ 1.2; one whose angle straddles zero
(the Xianshuihe) needs T/N ≤ 1. The effective normal stress is capped at
−10 MPa in both the interseismic and dynamic phases.
